messages.author: 2a7f346506a3e9ff
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: GSOC
parts:
On Sun, Jan 19, 2014 at 2:54 PM, Ben Goodrich <goodri...@gmail.com> wrote:
On Saturday, March 9, 2013 4:48:18 PM UTC-5, Ben Goodrich wrote:
Last year we briefly mentioned the possibility of Stan participating in Google's Summer of Code. If we actually intend to do that, we should come up with a list of manageable projects ASAP because rumor has it that the 2013 call for proposals is imminent.

It is next year now. The GSOC mentoring organization proposals are due the first couple weeks of February if we want to do this

https://www.google-melange.com/gsoc/document/show/gsoc_program/google/gsoc2014/help_page#2._What_should_a_mentoring_organization
Participating would be a great idea.
Probably need to focus on projects that do not actually involve much statistics.

I think it's good to provide a mix.  Some of these projects get senior undergrads and graduate students as participants so it's not strictly required that they be non-statistical.  Regardless, they should be concrete projects with limited scope.  Here are a couple of ideas:

- More flexible initialization by adding an "initialization" model block
- Optimized implementations of more distributions, e.g., make Geo BUGS models easier/faster in Stan
- Vectorization of multivariate distributions
- Implement L-BFGS and start unit testing optimization
- Parallelization

There are certainly more possibilities.  We should make a page on the wiki to keep track of ideas.

Cheers,
Marcus

Ben

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: GSOC
parts:
On Monday, January 20, 2014 1:07:29 PM UTC-5, Bob Carpenter wrote:
OK, do any three people want to volunteer?
Or can all of the admins and mentors be the
same person?  I don't even have the patience to read
through their application materials.

The administrator and the backup administrator have to be different people in case one is hit by a bus. The mentors can overlap in all kinds of ways.

The first hurdle we have to clear is for Google to accept us as a mentoring organization. If that happens, then we get a bunch of student applications to read in March.

In my experience, 3 months is rarely enough time
for even a good student to be a net win in terms
of the effort you have to put in versus the code
you get out.  Peter and Yuanjun were both pleasant
exceptions!

We need more exceptions. But the 3 month thing is why I'm not too optimistic about largely stats projects (although we should list them if we decide to apply). But I could imagine a talented student being able to do
  • HTML interface to Stan models compiled via pnacl or emscripten
  • Java interface
  • One or more of the alternate parser things (JSON, csv, file-backed, multiple data statements, etc.)
  • initialization {} block
  • Turning off more checks if NDEBUG is defined
  • Implement multidimensional_thing ~ distribution(scalar, scalar, ...); 
  • L-BFGS-B
And maybe some others.

Ben

I already said I would be the administrator or backup administrator, which is not much of a commitment. But we need mentors (plural) since each GSOC student-project requires a mentor. We will probably get at most a few project slots, but we can't accept students and then leave them hanging. So we really need to decide if we have enough mentoring commitment. Basically, what would you be willing to do this summer if it only required you to do half the work (via mentoring a student) but would be unwilling to do if you had to do all the work?

I've put the outline of a few projects up at

https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/wiki/GSOC2014Ideas

Feel free to expand upon them or add new ones or list yourself as a mentor of an idea in the idea header.

Ben
